sections.content: How many people are "stonemasons and related trades"?

10,410 people

were counted on the census as "stonemasons and related trades" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Stonemasons set up and repair structures of stone and similar materials and cut, shape and polish granite, marble, slate and other stone for building, ornamental and other purposes.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "stonemasons and related trades" there were more men than women (97.9% compared with 2.1%).

This means "stonemasons and related trades" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled construction and building trades".

Men made up 97.9% and women made up 2.1% of "stonemasons and related trades"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "stonemasons and related trades" included:

  • welding trades
  • vehicle body builders and repairers
  • road construction operatives

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "stonemasons and related trades" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "stonemasons and related trades", 12.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "stonemasons and related trades" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "stonemasons and related trades" included:

  • electrical and electronic trades (other)
  • routine inspectors and testers
  • plastics process operatives

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "stonemasons and related trades", 8.2% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (85.8% compared with 14.2%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (51.5%) than an employee (48.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Cornwall, this is in the same region of the South West.
